[34mInvestigated:[0m The compound formatter in src/index.ts (fmtCompound, the format() dispatch, and the compound option type) and the compound tests in src/format.test.ts. The README's Time Format Written-Out and Input Formats sections, where no compound documentation existed before this work. The git history showing commits 6b7b16e and 4dc0103.

[33mLearned:[0m fmtCompound uses whole seconds only, so sub-second remainders are dropped and -500 returns "0s" without a sign, because the zero-parts early return happens before the sign is applied. Compound output is space-separated and can include a day unit (e.g. "1d 1h 1m 1s"), which the Go deploy-log consumer rejects. The parse() length guard runs before trimming, and its limit (100) does not match its error message (99).

[32mCompleted:[0m A "Compound Format" section was added to README.md with examples and the precedence rule. src/format.test.ts gained cases for 59999, 86399999, 1500.7, -90061000, and 365 days, plus Infinity and -Infinity throwing in compound mode. The work is committed as 99094c3 on feat/compound-format and has not been pushed. The full jest suite passes with 187 tests, and tsc and biome are clean.

[35mNext Steps:[0m The compound output format is still the current ParseDuration-incompatible version. The planned rework would glue the parts and use hours as the largest unit (e.g. 25h30m), which would also require updating the README and tests. This is pending the user's decision on whether to do it before review.

[36mNotes:[0m The README and tests document the behavior the code has today. If the ParseDuration-compatible rework goes ahead, both the README section and the compound test table will need to change with it. The parse() length-guard mismatch was left alone as out of scope.
